title: Plan a Sprint by capacity and keep it honest

say: Plan a Sprint by capacity, and keep it honest.
This is the video for module 2 of Agile and Scrum in Practice.
Many teams perform the Scrum events without getting the benefits. Running Scrum well starts with an ordered backlog and an honest forecast.

panel.heading: Knowing the events is not enough
items: A forecast based on real capacity
A Definition of Done that protects quality
Early warning when a Sprint drifts

say: Then a clear Definition of Done protects quality, and a simple chart warns you early when a Sprint is drifting. Let us walk through each one.

say: For example, a 5-person team is building a WhatsApp ordering system for Tola's bakery in Ibadan. Tola is the Product Owner. She orders the backlog by value: first the menu with prices, then placing an order, then paying by transfer.

panel.heading: Tola's bakery ordering backlog
items: Top items small enough for one Sprint
Split items that are too big

say: Items at the top must be small and clear enough to finish in one Sprint. Lower items can stay rough ideas.

items: Top items small enough for one Sprint

say: Paying by transfer is too big, so the team splits it in two: show bank details and an order reference, then Tola confirms payment.

say: They size items with Planning Poker. Everyone shows a number at once, on a scale like 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. The highest and lowest explain, and the team votes again. The talk exposes hidden work.

say: The top five items total 3, 5, 2, 5 and 3. That is 18 points.

say: For example, Chidi's team has 5 Developers in a 10-day Sprint. That is 50 person-days.
One day is a public holiday, which removes 5. Ada has 2 days of leave. That leaves 43.
43 divided by 50 is 86% of a normal Sprint.
Their last three Sprints delivered 21, 18 and 24 points. The average, called velocity, is 21.
So the forecast is 21 times 0.86, about 18 points, not 21. The Product Owner cannot force more in.
Use velocity only to forecast your own team. Never compare or reward it between teams, or estimates inflate.

panel.heading: Forecast from real capacity
panel.rule: The Developers decide how much they take on.

say: Sprint Planning also produces one Sprint Goal. Finish tickets 14 to 22 is weak. It names work, not value.

panel.heading: Weak goal versus strong goal
right: Customers pay by transfer, get confirmed
Director sees weekly sales on her phone

say: Customers can pay by transfer and get confirmation is strong. It names a user and a checkable result, so the team can swap items and still meet it.

panel.heading: Weak goal versus strong goal
right: Customers pay by transfer, get confirmed
Director sees weekly sales on her phone

say: The Definition of Done is the quality bar. If an item misses it, it is not shown as done. It goes back to the backlog.
Keep it short and checkable. Five honest checks beat twenty that nobody follows.
And never put phone numbers, BVN or payment screenshots on a board card. Use an order reference, in line with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.

panel.heading: Tola's Definition of Done
items: Works on a low-cost Android on slow 3G
Tested by someone other than the builder
No customer personal data in logs
Wording checked by the Product Owner

say: A burndown chart plots the work remaining against the days. For example, Halima's team planned 40 points in a 10-day Sprint. That is 4 points a day, so by day 5, 20 should remain.

cards.d: 40 points over 10 days is 4 a day. By day 5, 20 points should remain.
34 points remain: 14 behind. At 1.2 a day, 28 points would be left undone.
Three items wait for one API key. Escalate it, and move an 8-point item back to the backlog.

say: But 34 remain. They are 14 points behind. At their pace, 28 points would be left undone.

say: At the next Daily Scrum, she asks what is blocking work. Three items wait for one API key from a partner bank. They escalate it that morning, and the Product Owner moves an 8-point item back to the backlog, while keeping the Sprint Goal.
The chart fixed nothing alone. It started the right talk on day 5 instead of day 10.

say: To remember. Order the backlog and split big items. Forecast with velocity adjusted for real capacity. Keep the Daily Scrum to 15 minutes and solve problems after it.
Done means it meets the Definition of Done. And end every Retrospective with one or two actions, each with an owner and a date.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Order the backlog; split big items
Forecast with velocity adjusted for capacity
Daily Scrum is 15 minutes; solve problems after
Done means it meets the Definition of Done
End each Retrospective with one or two actions

say: Your tasks: set up your backlog and a free board, run a one-week mini-Sprint with a capacity calculation, then draw its burndown and score it against the healthy signals.
